findings.reason: The approved fd-bl01 page requires fd-l01, whose current items define a periodic Leray-projected residual and a smooth periodic comparison estimate. Neither matches the assigned bounded-domain, full-momentum-residual, common-wall estimate or capillary model; no assigned item currently depends on an fd-l01 item. The verified edge record establishes readiness, not a logical use. The owner must decide whether to remove or reclassify this page requirement, or provide an earlier supplier with the bounded common-wall interface.

The common-wall and lift clauses use boundary traces for fields in C²(D), which does not ensure a classical boundary trace. The item also uses “C² domain” without defining its boundary charts, and calls φ a velocity potential without defining the velocity as ∇φ. Specify the boundary regularity, trace convention and potential relation.

In step 2.1, F3 is scalar L² Cauchy–Schwarz but the proof applies it to the vector pairing e·r. State the L²(D;R³) inner product and use the applicable inner-product Cauchy–Schwarz supplier, or give the pointwise Euclidean bound followed by scalar L² Cauchy–Schwarz. F7 also applies thm-of-square-roots to real numbers without stating the complete-ordered-field hypothesis; explicitly instantiate it using thm-reals-cauchy-complete.

F2 and step 1.1 use thm-of-square-roots for real radicands without stating that R is a complete ordered field; identify the bridge, such as thm-reals-cauchy-complete. In step 3.1, E′=0 does not by itself establish that E is constant; cite and use cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant, whose interval and continuity hypotheses can be checked here.

The mode formula uses x∈T_λ inside kx without defining the representative convention. The proof also asserts 2π-periodicity and smoothness, while the cited gravity-mode theorem states only C² spatial and C¹ time regularity on real coordinates. Cite or prove periodicity (for example via thm-sine-cosine-zero-sets-and-fundamental-period), define the torus phase using representatives, and support the stated smoothness.
